messages:
sara-support: Customer reported p99 token latency jumped from 120ms -> 1.2s around 10:12 UTC, only for requests from EU users hitting the hosted API. Seeing lots of backend time in our logs. Anyone else?
ryan-sre: saw alerts. Traces look like normal until egress then an unexpected hop to us-east-1 before returning to eu-west-1. That explains extra RTT.
ana ?: (typo)
ana: nvm
ana: can you paste a sample trace id?
ryan-sre: trace: trace-0a1b2c3d4e – excerpt:
```
# span timeline
client -> edge-eu (ingest)
edge-eu -> router-eu (0-12ms)
router-eu -> us-east-1/egress-node (240-480ms)
us-east-1 -> model-eu (480-760ms)
```
ryan-sre: router-eu forwarded to an egress in us-east-1, then came back. That double travel is the culprit.
ana: and the egress node's tags show `region=us-east-1, pool=shared-burst` while the request model is available in eu pools.
janet-cs: customers are seeing timeouts in their dashboards too, multiple tickets. We need mitigation ASAP.
ana: quick check — any recent routing policy rollout? Ops bot?
ops-bot: deploy: routing-service v4.21.0 promoted to stable at 2026-11-03T09:50:12Z by ci/cd (canary previously).
ryan-sre: that aligns with the timeline. v4.21 introduced `fallback_to_compatible_region` to reduce errors; seems to prefer lower-cost pool if region match fuzzy. Might be matching on model name prefix only.
mike-devex: if matching is fuzzy, requests for `redwood-instruct-v2` might match `redwood-instruct-v2-legacy` in us-east pool.
nana: reproduced locally: send request with header `X-Model: redwood-instruct-v2` and `prefer_region: eu-west-1`, router still picks us-east because `compatible_variant: true` rule weight > region preference.
ryan-sre: posted a snippet of the decision log from router for one request:
```
decision: route_candidates = [eu-pool-1(weight=80), us-pool-shared(weight=60)]
score(calc) = region_score * 0.4 + cost_score * 0.6
region_score(eu-pool-1)=0.9, cost_score=0.2 -> total 0.46
region_score(us-pool)=0.3, cost_score=0.9 -> total 0.66 -> selected
```
ryan-sre: so cost weight is dominating and causing cross-region hop.
janet-cs: customers are blocked; recommend immediate rollback to old routing or patch to increase region weight. Which is faster?
nana: quick mitigation: set `prefer_region` hard constraint for hosted-production until we patch weights. Can be flipped via feature flag in config-store.
mike-devex: steps to repro for support engineering:
1) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "X-Model: redwood-instruct-v2" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate?prefer_region=eu-west-1
2) check `x-routing-path` header in response for egress node id
3) correlate with traces in honeycomb using trace id header `x-trace-id`

janet-cs: I'll add an interim note to affected tickets with repro and expected mitigation steps.
ryan-sre: I'm pushing a hotfix PR to bump region weight from 0.4 -> 0.8 and to treat `prefer_region` as hard preference when present. If tests pass I'll deploy to canary now.
ops-bot: canary deploy started: routing-service v4.21.1-canary at 2026-11-03T10:05:03Z
ana: monitoring p99 on canary traffic now. Initial telemetry looks good (p99 reduced back to ~140ms for EU).
janet-cs: customers notified. I'll keep tickets open until stable deploy.
ryan-sre: after canary green, I'll roll to stable and add an alert that surfaces unexpected inter-region egress with sample traces. Also creating an eval to check variant matching rules.
janet-cs: thanks team — keep me posted. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: stable deploy routing-service v4.21.1 promoted at 2026-11-03T10:22:11Z
ryan-sre: stable is up, region-weight fix in place. Closing incident once all tickets ack.
janet-cs: confirming with two affected customers — both report latency back to normal. Closing. :white_check_mark:
